    AI Overview
    A Blue Alert is a rapid notification system used to inform the public and law enforcement when a suspect is wanted for killing, seriously injuring, or posing an imminent, credible threat to a law enforcement officer. It may also be issued if an officer is missing in the line of duty. 
    Key Aspects of a Blue Alert: 
    • Purpose: To quickly share suspect information (like vehicles or descriptions) to aid in apprehension and protect public safety.
    • Mechanism: Information is transmitted via wireless devices (cell phones), the Emergency Alert System (EAS), and media outlets.
    • National Scope: Established by Congress in 2015, the National Blue Alert Network supports plans in over 37 states.
    • Criteria: Generally, the suspect must be considered "armed and dangerous," with local law enforcement confirming the threat or injury. 
    These alerts function similarly to AMBER Alerts but are specific to law enforcement targets.
